name: LGBT National Help Center
summary: Peer support and local resources for LGBTQ+ individuals through phone and online chat.

sections.title: About the LGBT National Help Center
sections.text: The LGBT National Help Center provides free and confidential peer support and local resources for LGBTQ+ individuals, their families, and allies. Operating since 1996, the Help Center runs three specialized phone lines and online chat services staffed by trained volunteers from the LGBTQ+ community. The organization serves people of all ages who are looking for a safe space to talk about their identity, struggles, coming out process, or any issues related to being LGBTQ+.

sections.title: Phone Lines and Services
sections.text: The LGBT National Hotline (1-888-843-4564) serves all ages and provides peer support, information, and local resources. The LGBT National Youth Talkline (1-800-246-7743) specifically serves youth ages 25 and under with peer support from young volunteers who understand the unique challenges LGBTQ+ youth face. The LGBT National Senior Hotline (1-888-234-7243) provides support for LGBTQ+ seniors who may face isolation and unique challenges. All lines connect callers with trained peer volunteers.

sections.title: Who Contacts the Help Center
sections.text: People contact the Help Center for many reasons: questioning their sexual orientation or gender identity, preparing to come out, dealing with family rejection or acceptance, navigating relationships, experiencing discrimination or harassment, feeling isolated or alone, seeking LGBTQ+-friendly resources in their area, or simply wanting to talk to someone who understands. Parents and family members also call seeking support and information to help them understand and support LGBTQ+ loved ones.

sections.title: How to Reach the Help Center
sections.text: Call the main Hotline at 1-888-843-4564, the Youth Talkline at 1-800-246-7743, or the Senior Hotline at 1-888-234-7243. Check the website for current hours as they vary by day. Online chat is available through lgbthotline.org. All services are free and confidential. Volunteers can provide peer support, information about LGBTQ+ topics, and connections to local resources including support groups, community centers, and LGBTQ+-affirming service providers.

sections.title: Peer Support Approach
sections.text: The LGBT National Help Center uses a peer support model, meaning volunteers are members of the LGBTQ+ community who have been trained to provide compassionate, non-judgmental support. Peer volunteers understand firsthand the experiences and challenges of being LGBTQ+ in today's world. This shared experience creates a unique connection and helps callers feel truly understood. Volunteers listen, provide information, and help callers explore their feelings and options without pushing any particular path.
